Final Thoughts: Which Galapagos Experience Is Right for You?
When deciding between a cruise or a hotel for your Galapagos adventure, it is important to reflect on what matters most to you. Whether you prefer the adventure of visiting remote islands on a cruise or the flexibility of a hotel stay, the Galapagos Islands promise an unforgettable immersive experience. Choosing the Right Galapagos Boat Tour: Small Yacht vs. Cruise Ship
When traveling to the Islands, choosing the best boat for Galapagos tours is essential to getting the most out of the magnificent wildlife and landscapes. Depending on your travel style, It is important to consider the ship size and determine if you prefer the intimacy of a smaller yacht or the extra amenities of a larger cruise ship.
Comparing Galapagos Boat Options: Small Yachts vs. Cruise Ships
Let's dive into the specific benefits of the Galapagos small boat vs. big boat!
Advantages of Small Yachts
Close-Knit Atmosphere and Personal Connections Small yachts create an intimate setting, making it easier to connect with fellow passengers and naturalist guides . These smaller groups allow for more personalized experiences, deeper conversations with naturalist guides, and unique opportunities to immerse yourself in the Galapagos' natural beauty.
Greater Wildlife Encounters Traveling on a smaller yacht , it is easier for the crew to maneuver when there are wildlife encounters happening near you. Chase whales on the horizon or watch the dolphins jump along with the ship as you sail, you’ll be so close to the action!
More Time in Remote Galapagos Sites Since small yachts can anchor closer to the islands and groups are smaller, you have the opportunity to spend more time exploring the Islands and get there faster. Enjoy quieter excursions for those really seeking seclusion and immersion in the islands’ natural beauty.
Advantages of Cruise Ships and Large Boats
Enhanced Stability and Comfort Larger cruise ships offer more stability, reducing seasickness and providing a smoother sailing experience. Spacious cabins, large decks, large dining areas, and well-designed interiors make these ships a comfortable option for travelers who prioritize a relaxed journey with extra onboard options.
Expanded Amenities and Social Spaces With extra amenities, larger cruise ships typically offer more elaborate dining services, larger social lounges, and more entertainment options. This option is ideal for travelers who enjoy socializing and prefer a variety of onboard activities.
Flexible Itinerary Choices and Organized Excursions While all Galapagos cruises have structured itineraries, larger cruise ships offer more disembarkation options and a wider variety of activities that cater to everyone's preferences, like snorkeling, kayaking, paddleboarding, or glass bottom boats! This is perfect for travelers who enjoy a planned yet flexible approach to their adventures.
Choosing Your Perfect Galapagos Boat: Small Yacht vs. Cruise Ship
Each and every Galapagos boat tour option offers unique benefits so you can find the perfect trip that is suited to your travel style. It is important to consider your priorities, whether that be intimacy, adventure, or making new friendships.
What to Consider:
Couples seeking romance and privacy: Opt for a small yacht with fewer passengers and an intimate ambiance.
Families or groups traveling with children: Choose a cruise ship with a multitude of family-friendly amenities and plenty of space.
Solo adventurers: A cruise ship offers opportunities to meet fellow travelers and socialize in shared spaces.
Eco-conscious travelers: Select either! All boats must follow strict environmental standards in Galapagos.
Sustainable Travel in the Galapagos
Both small yachts and cruise ships implement sustainable tourism practices on all expeditions as the Galapagos National Park’s regulations prioritize the protection of the Islands, which helps you to feel good knowing that any tour you pick is an eco-friendly choice!
All boats are required to recycle all garbage as the National Park has implemented the mission of zero trash in the Islands
There are multiple annual environmental inspections, at both local and international levels, that all ships are required to pass
The Galapagos National Park has visitor limitations, which serve to protect wildlife and ecosystems
Luckily, all tour boats in the Galapagos promote environmental efforts and responsibility due to the laws of the National Park
Additionally, by traveling with us at Galapagos Islands.Travel, you are supporting local environmental protection efforts in Ecuador and the Galapagos Islands!
The Galapagos, as a destination, is one of the most environmentally-conscious places to travel in the world, so you can breathe easy knowing that you’re helping take care of the planet.
Embark on Your Ideal Galapagos Adventure
Choosing the perfect boat for your Galapagos journey is important, and we are here to help you find your perfect match! Whether you choose a small yacht or a larger cruise ship , unforgettable memories await you in the Galapagos Islands.
Galapagos Islands boat comparison in a nutshell:
Small yachts offer a personalized experience, more wildlife encounter opportunities, and you’ll spend more time exploring remote parts of the Islands
Larger cruise ships offer greater stability and comfort, more amenities, and a more flexible itinerary with more activity options
Explore the largest collection of the best Galapagos cruises here with Galapagos Islands.Travel, or contact a Voyagers Travel Company advisor for personalized guidance .
Frequently Asked Questions About Choosing a Galapagos Boat
Q: What are the maximum capacities of the small yachts and large cruise ships?
A: Small yachts typically have a maximum of 16 passengers, while larger cruise ships cannot exceed a capacity of 100 passengers. So, while the larger cruise ships are big, they still have a relatively small amount of passengers aboard. There are also plenty of boat options with passenger capacities somewhere in the middle!
Q: Are small yachts safe for Galapagos tours?
A: Yes! All boats of all sizes in the Galapagos need to follow strict guidelines to be able to sail within the Galapagos marine preserve. On every tour there are passenger limits, certified naturalists that are trained in wildlife safety, and experienced crew trained in Galapagos navigation.
Q: How stable are Galapagos cruise ships?
A: Larger cruise ships in the Galapagos Islands are very stable, and are the preferred option for those prone to seasickness. While the Galapagos seas are generally calm, the added size and weight of cruise ships reduce motion, offering a smoother experience compared to smaller vessels. If you do prefer a smaller boat, choosing a catamaran or trimaran have added stability and can ease feelings of seasickness. If seasickness is a major concern, it is recommended to travel between January and June, when the seas are calmer.
Q: What is the environmental impact of a Galapagos cruise?
A: Both small yachts and larger cruise ships operate under strict Galapagos National Park guidelines to minimize environmental impact. All boats must pass the local National Park Environmental Inspection as well as obtain the international IOPP environmental certificate annually to be able to operate in the Galapagos, which contribute to protecting the islands’ unique ecosystems.
Q: Can small yachts visit all Galapagos visitor sites?
A: Yes! Both small yachts and large cruise ships have access to all visitor points in the whole archipelago, while adhering to the National Park-approved itinerary, regulations on permitted landing sites, and group sizes.
Q: Do Galapagos cruise ships offer a flexible schedule?
A: Larger cruise ships provide a structured, yet varied schedule that allows passengers to choose among activities like snorkeling, hiking, and wildlife viewing. However, all ships follow a strict schedule for all visitor sites, that is approved by the National Park in advance.
Q: How does group size impact the Galapagos experience?
A: Smaller groups, typically on small yachts, allow for a more personal and immersive experience. Larger cruise ships, with more passengers, still maintain limited group sizes on excursions due to Galapagos National Park regulations, ensuring a quality experience regardless of boat size.

Best Time to Visit the Galapagos Islands
The Galapagos Islands offer unique wildlife and activities year-round. The best time to visit Galapagos depends on your interests, whether you’re a wildlife lover, a diving enthusiast, or simply looking for perfect weather.
With two distinct seasons—the Warm, Wet Season ( December to June ) and the Cool, Dry Season ( July to November )—each month brings unique natural wonders to discover.
Galapagos Seasons: Month-by-Month Highlights
Every month in the Galapagos brings unique opportunities to witness nature’s wonders. Whether you’re planning your trip around wildlife encounters, calm seas, or vibrant landscapes, there’s never a wrong time to visit this year-round destination. The key to choosing the best time to go to Galapagos depends on your interests, from snorkeling with playful sea lions to observing iconic species during their courtship rituals.
If you want to know when to visit Galapagos islands to experience seasonal highlights, check out our Galapagos visitor sites map .
The Best Time to Buy Your Galapagos Tour
So you figured out when you want to travel, but when is the best time to buy you Galapagos Islands tour? We have the answers for you right here so you can learn more about the best time for you to buy!
Warm, Wet Season: December to June
If you’re wondering about the best time of year to visit Galapagos, the warm, wet season offers lush landscapes, warmer waters, and incredible wildlife activity. This is an ideal time for snorkeling and diving, with calm seas, excellent visibility, and a vibrant underwater world teeming with life.
Cool, Dry Season: July to November
The cool, dry season transforms the Galapagos into a diver’s paradise. Cooler water temperatures, driven by the Humboldt Current, attract whale sharks, sea lions, and large schools of fish. Though the waters are cooler, nutrient-rich currents create exceptional opportunities for diving enthusiasts seeking to observe vibrant marine life, making it the best time to go to the Galapagos for diving enthusiasts.
When to Visit: Tailoring Your Trip to Your Interests
Wildlife Lovers
The Galapagos Islands offer year-round wildlife encounters, but:
December to June: Lush landscapes and excellent opportunities to see tortoises hatching, marine iguana nesting season, and courtship displays.
July to November: Cooler waters attract marine life like penguins, sea lions, and whale sharks.
Diving and Snorkeling Enthusiasts
Warm Season (December–May): Warmer, calmer seas with excellent underwater visibility. Ideal for snorkeling.
Dry Season (June–November): Cooler, nutrient-rich waters bring currents that attract whale sharks, hammerhead sharks, and large schools of fish.
Families and Relaxed Travelers
December to May offers calmer seas, making travel between islands more comfortable. Perfect for families with kids.
You’ve decided when to visit the Galapagos Islands, but when is the best time to book your tour? Planning ahead can help you secure the best deals, preferred dates, and top-rated accommodations.

Weather in the Galapagos Islands
The Galapagos enjoys pleasant weather year-round thanks to its position on the equator. Air temperatures range between 70°F (21°C) and 80°F (27°C), with slight variations between seasons.
For a detailed breakdown of Galapagos weather and seasonal conditions, visit our Galapagos weather guide .

There’s no single “best time” to go to the Galapagos Islands—every month offers something unique. Whether you’re watching sea lions play in July or witnessing blue-footed booby courtship dances in April, the islands promise unforgettable encounters with nature.

FAQs: When to Visit the Galapagos Islands
Q: What is the best time to go to the Galapagos?
A: There’s no bad time to visit! However, December to June offers warmer weather and calm seas, while July to November brings cooler waters with abundant marine life. The best time of year to go to the Galapagos islands depends on your interests.
Q: When is the best time to see Galapagos wildlife?
A: Wildlife is present year-round, but breeding and nesting vary by species and season.
Q: Is the Galapagos crowded during peak season?
A: The Galapagos National Park limits visitors to protect the environment, ensuring a relaxed experience even during peak travel months.
Q: What is the best season for diving in the Galapagos?
A: The best time to go to the Galapagos for calm waters and clear visibility is between December and May. For exciting encounters with whale sharks and hammerheads, June to November is ideal. Learn more about our Diving Tours in the Galapagos .

How to Get to the Galapagos Islands: A Quick Guide for Travelers
A trip to the Galapagos Islands is the ultimate bucket-list getaway for any avid nature enthusiast, adventure seeker, or eco-conscious traveler. However, the remote location can make travel planning challenging.
So, how do you get to the Galapagos Islands? The good news is that Galapagos Islands.Travel has the expertise and knowledge needed to ensure your journey is smooth and hassle-free. In this quick guide on how to get to the Galapagos, we’ll walk you through the essential details and provide tips to ensure a seamless journey.
Where Are the Galapagos Islands?
The Galapagos Islands are located in the Pacific Ocean, approximately 600 miles off the coast of Ecuador. These volcanic outcroppings are world-renowned for their unique biodiversity, and you’ll find species here that can’t be seen anywhere else on Earth. The Galapagos Islands offer a rare glimpse into the natural world, from giant tortoises to playful sea lions.
Aside from the resident wildlife, visitors are drawn to the islands by:
World-class adventure experiences such as kayaking, snorkeling & horseback riding.
Out-of-this-world scuba diving experiences in crystal-clear waters.
Leading eco-tourism practices that prioritize conservation and sustainability .
Your Gateway to the Galapagos: Ecuador
Transiting through Ecuador is the norm because there are no direct connections to the islands from any other country. Flights to the Galapagos depart regularly from the international gateways of Quito (UIO) and Guayaquil (GYE), each of which offers distinct benefits:
Quito: Ecuador's high-altitude capital offers a rich cultural experience complete with charming streets and UNESCO-protected colonial architecture. Sitting at nearly 10,000 feet above sea level, visitors can expect stunning Andean landscapes, vibrant markets, and plenty of opportunities to explore museums and galleries.
Guayaquil: As a coastal city, Guayaquil is the most practical choice for travelers looking for quick and easy connections to the islands. The warm climate makes it a relaxing place to acclimatize before heading to the Galapagos, and there’s a more laid-back vibe here than in the bustling capital.
At Galapagos Islands.Travel, we can assist with every aspect of your pre-trip planning—from international flights and Ecuador city stays to how to get to the Galapagos Islands and the best excursions to take once you arrive. With over 20 years of experience, we specialize in personalized travel planning and offer various travel packages to suit all preferences.
Essential Tips for Traveling to the Galapagos
Once you’ve decided how to get to Galapagos and booked your connections and hotel stays, it’s time to start your holiday countdown! Here are a few essential tips to help you prepare:
Preparation and documentation: You don’t need a visa for Ecuador for visits under 90 days. However, you’ll need to fill out an INGALA Transit Control Card and pay the Galapagos National Park entrance fee , which helps support local conservation efforts.
Packing: Light, breathable clothing is ideal for the tropical climate. Don’t forget essentials like eco-friendly sunscreen, waterproof gear, and sturdy shoes for hiking and exploring.
Eco-Responsibility: The Galapagos Islands are a protected environment, so you must follow biosecurity protocols and sustainability initiatives that help preserve the unique ecosystem.
Currency: The Galapagos Islands and Ecuador both use the US Dollar. While credit cards are widely accepted in Ecuador, the Galapagos Islands are primarily cash-based, so it is advisable to carry plenty with you.
Travel insurance: We strongly recommend you purchase comprehensive travel insurance that covers medical emergencies, trip cancellations, and unexpected events.
Health precautions: Consult your healthcare provider to ensure you're up-to-date on routine vaccines and discuss any additional precautions based on your specific itinerary.
Local customs: While English is widely spoken, learning a few basic Spanish phrases will enhance your interactions and demonstrate your respect for the local culture.
Before you set off, double-check our Galapagos trip checklist to ensure you have covered all bases.
Getting to the Galapagos Islands
You can reach the islands by either air or sea, but flying is the most common and practical method:
How to get to Galapagos by air: Domestic flights from Quito or Guayaquil land at Baltra (GPS) or San Cristóbal (SCY) airports. Flights typically take around 2-2.5 hours.
How to get to Galapagos by sea: There are no tourist boats that connect the mainland with the islands. Galapagos expedition-style cruises offer an immersive experience to your island adventure, but they only operate within the archipelago.

FAQ: Common Questions About Traveling to the Galapagos
Q: How do I get to the Galapagos Islands?
A: To reach the Galapagos Islands, travelers must first fly to Ecuador , arriving at either Quito (Mariscal Sucre International Airport) or Guayaquil (José Joaquín de Olmedo International Airport). From there, domestic flights are available to the main airports in the Galapagos: Baltra (near Santa Cruz Island) or San Cristóbal.
Q: Can you fly directly to the Galapagos Islands?
A: No, there are no direct international connections. Flights to Galapagos depart only from mainland Ecuador.
Q: What documents do I need to travel to the Galapagos?
A: You will need a valid passport and an INGALA Transit Control Card. You’ll also need to pay the Galapagos National Park entrance fee .
Q: Which airport is best to fly into in the Galapagos?
A: The best Galapagos flights will vary depending on your itinerary and preferred activities. Baltra Airport is commonly used by island hopping and cruise passengers, while San Cristóbal Airport is generally preferred by travelers staying on the islands.
Q: What’s the best time to visit the Galapagos Islands?
A: The islands can be visited year-round, although the best time to visit the Galapagos depends on your interests and priorities. December to May offers warmer weather and calmer seas, while the cooler months from June to November feature more active wildlife.
Q: What can I bring to the Galapagos Islands?
A: When considering what to pack for your Galapagos adventure , remember that items harmful to the environment are prohibited. So, be sure to pack eco-friendly sunscreen. Sturdy footwear, waterproof gear, and extra memory cards and batteries for your camera are also recommended.
Q: Do I need a guide to explore the Galapagos?
A: Yes, most activities within the Galapagos National Park require a certified guide. This is both for your safety and to ensure that sustainable tourism and conservation best practices are followed, enabling the Galapagos’ unique natural wonder to be preserved for future generations.

The Enchanted Archipelago is renowned as an iconic tourist destination – and with good reason. It features some of the world’s most unique and endemic wildlife species, wonderful beaches that continually rank among the world’s best. This living laboratory will offer its visitors a spectacle to be admired, a daily story that will turn this journey into a story to forever be told.
A trip to the Galapagos Islands will be the journey of your lifetime. The archipelago is blessed with pleasant weather all year round, so there is no “best” time to visit the precious islands. However, you may consider factors such as high season vs. low season and the climate, and some other factors, best explained in our when to go to the Galapagos Islands article.
Where are the Galapagos Islands?
The Archipelago is a group of 19 islands, 13 large and 6 small, and dozens of islets and rocks that cover an area of over 17,000 square miles. Its closest point to the mainland is off 600 miles from the West coast of Ecuador in South America
What can I do in Galapagos?
The Galapagos Islands offers everyone the possibility to enjoy a great variety of activities for all ages, interests, and fitness, ranging from the contemplative to the adventurous, and knowing that in everything you do you will experience the best of the wildlife and nature.
Trekking
By far the most popular activity in the archipelago, trekking in the Galapagos brings the best opportunity to take some amazing pictures of the wildlife and landscapes. You and a small party will be led by a naturalist guide appointed by the Galapagos National Park through trails brimming with wonderful life and awe-inspiring views.
Snorkeling
Most tours include snorkeling, the easiest and most practical way to experience the amazing underwater world of Galapagos. Even from the dinghy, you can already see some curious sea lions and penguins watching you coming closer. Enter the waters, and you’ll be overwhelmed by the abundance of marine life surrounding you.
Kayaking
Paddling alongside the island’s shore and observe many birds nesting in the tree branches, schools of baby rays and sharks, as well as other marine life enjoying the tranquil turquoise waters of Galapagos. Discover the hidden beauty of lagoons surrounded by mangrove forest while kayaking at leisure.
Scuba-Diving
In the Galapagos, you can see so many water species and so close; and scuba diving is, without a doubt, the best and most rewarding underwater experience available. Just picture yourself swimming along schools of rays, and admiring really close their graceful movements and shapes, and sea lions wanting to play with the calm turtles who are trying to eat some algae off the rocks. View all of our Diving Tours
Galapagos Natural Wonders
Flora & Fauna of the Galapagos
The Galapagos are a naturalist’s dream, filled with a diverse array of plant and animal life unique in the world. This includes such exotic flora and fauna as giant cacti, finches, flightless cormorants, and the famed giant tortoise, whose average lifespan of 100 years makes it the longest living vertebrate on earth. Rumor has it that there may even be a “great-grandpa” tortoise that hatched around the time Darwin arrived at the islands.
Underwater World
The Galapagos marine animals include more than 2,900 species, 25% percent of which are endemic, meaning that they are found nowhere else on Earth. Among the most notable species are the Galapagos penguins (the only penguin species native to the Northern Hemisphere), Galapagos sea lions, marine iguanas, whales, hammerhead sharks and whale sharks.
The Galapagos are a marvel of geological activity . These volcanic islands are relatively new in the grand scheme of things (Isabela and Fernandina, the biggest islands, are said to be less than one million years old). Their formation occurred on the seafloor, at which point three tectonic plates converge and produce volcanic processes that continue to this day.
Galapagos History
If you are interested in who first set foot on the islands -whether it was the Incas, refugees, pirates or seafarers - find out more about the human history of the Islands . Speaking of men on the Islands, Charles Darwin, was one of the first to visit as he was fascinated by the natural history of the archipelago .
Charles Darwin in the Galapagos
The name of Charles Darwin and his famous book the Origin of Species will forever be linked with the Galapagos Islands. Although he was only in the Galapagos for five weeks in 1835, it was the wildlife that he saw there that inspired him to develop his Theory of Evolution.
Visiting the Galapagos Islands will undoubtedly affect you deeply. Dram come true - The trip was extremely well organized. Info beforehand was detailed. The Infiniti yacht was lovely. We chose it because of ifs itinerary around the west side of Isabela Island. ... read more The cabins were spacious, food was 5-star level and beautifully served. Guides excellent. The staff was caring and did anything anybody wished for comfort. There were 19 passenfers and 14 staff + 2 guides. The progams started at 7 am with breakfast and ended at dinner at 7 pm. Guests have to be in good physical condition to enjoy the walks, snorkeling and kayacking. And moving in the tender back and forth between the boat and the shore requires agility. Weather is worth thinking about. We had 8 perfect days, but if it rains, it would be different. The length of 7 nights/8 days was optimal. Hotel in Quito (one night before and one night after the cruise was included) was great: Go Quito Hotel, a new hotel with a wonderful restaurant high up and a lovely spa, where I had an excellent massage at the end of the trip. It is far from the airport, 40 min drive, but worth it. Reading Darwin's account of his visit there in 1835 is very helpful and gives a prspective to why these islands are so special.

Katie,
I wanted to let you know that we greatly enjoyed our vacation to La Selva, Quito and the Galapagos islands. I had low expectations for two reasons: all the advertising photos showed gray overcast skies and people on Youtube have said the Galapagos isn't what you think it is. The landscape isn't great and because so many people go there it is hard to get photos of animals without people crowded near them. I found these pre-conceptions to be completely wrong. The skies were blue and sunny most of the time and there was plenty of room to take animal photos with no interference. The landscape was fascinating.
The guide who took us around in Quito for two days and picked us up at the airport upon our return from the Islands was absolutely outstanding. His name is Rocco. He is so easy to be around, he loves people, his English is easily understandable, and he is a fountain of information. He knows English, Spanish and German. He was so accommodating and helpful in many ways. This guy is a gem. Jorge was good too (he picked us up the night we arrived)
La Selva is a class act and our group of 8 had a fabulous guide who also spoke very understandable English. His name is Gabriel and he knows English and Spanish and is studying Chinese. We loved the room at La Selva. Paul and I went kayaking one afternoon on our own and when we got back to the dock, Paul had a hard time getting from the Kayak onto the dock. His phone got away from him and fell into the water. Fortunately we knew exactly where it was and one of the Native guides put on swim wear and dove into the water and retrieved it.
At Santa Cruz island we had a female park service guide whose English was difficult for me to understand. Two guides on the snorkeling/island exploration trips had Spanish accents so thick I could barely understand any of their English. The experience on the boats was a little rugged for me, but I managed to do okay and did some snorkeling along with the hiking. The birds and other animals are so easily accessible and visible and the scenery was stunning, especially on Bartolome.
I especially enjoyed Isabela Island and its laid back attitude and almost no one on the beach. The room at La Laguna was great even though the sink/counter area in the bathroom was more cramped than I liked. However, the room itself was very large and had two tables in it. We carried one over to a spot right outside the bathroom door and it served very well as a countertop for all my "stuff." The older you get the more stuff you need just to function.
The hotel in Old Town Quito was quite amazing, especially the rooftop bar. The room was a little small though and the hotel isn't situated close to where the street vendors (crafts, etc.) are situated. If Rocco hadn't taken us around at the shopping/vendor area we never would have known it was there in the area. But the staff at the hotel was super as they were everywhere we stayed. La Palma Polo really went the extra mile for us, not to mention giving us the chance to see a polo field, for heaven's sake. And the cabins there were enormous. I think they were built to accommodate families with their horses included in the room. (kidding)
It was overall a fabulous trip and worth every dime we paid for it. It was definitely the trip of a lifetime. You and the Voyagers Travel Company company put together a rather complicated package tour and it all worked seamlessly. Many thanks to all of you for your services!
Marie Kelsey and Paul Stein April, 2026

full_text:
Unforgettable Peru Tours and Guided Travel Packages
Embark on an unforgettable journey with our expertly curated Peru tours. From the breathtaking heights of Machu Picchu to the serene waters of Lake Titicaca, our customizable tour packages offer a perfect blend of adventure, culture, and history. Whether you’re seeking guided explorations of Peru’s iconic landmarks or unique add-ons to enhance your trip, we’ll create a personalized experience tailored just for you.
Start planning your dream vacation to Peru today and let us handle every detail of your journey!
Discover the must-see sites of Magical Peru!
Extend your Adventure with these Add-ons!
The highlights of Southamerica in one Amazing Trip!
Machu Picchu: South America’s Most Iconic Destination
Machu Picchu stands as Peru’s crown jewel, a breathtaking testament to the ingenuity of the Inca Empire. Perched high in the Andes, it offers travelers an unforgettable journey into history and nature.
Best Ways to Reach Machu Picchu: Getting to Machu Picchu can be a journey in itself, luckily there are options based on your sense of adventure and how much time you want to spend on the trip. If you want to arrive within a few hours, hop on a train from either Cusco, Urubamba, or Ollantaytambo. If you want to live more like the Incas, you can hike the iconic Inca Trail, which takes 3-5 days.
Don’t Miss: Key attractions at Machu Picchu include wandering through ancient temples and stone houses. Admire the ingenuity of the intricate terraces and aqueducts that allowed Incas to live on top of a mountain. Feel at peace as you embrace old traditions and their sacred harmony with nature.
Pro Tip: Consider hiring a local guide to learn about ancient Inca culture or bringing a map to better understand the historical significance of the ruins while staying on designated paths to best preserve the space for future travelers.
View our Machu Picchu Tour Packages Here!
Lima: Peru’s Cultural and Culinary Hub
Lima blends a rich cultural heritage with modern sophistication, making it a perfect starting point for any Peruvian tours. From world-class museums to exceptional cuisine, the capital city truly has it all.
Cultural Gems: For those looking for cultural immersion, you cannot miss the iconic museums and historical sites Peru has to offer, including Museo de Oro del Peru, Museo de la Nación, and Iglesia de San Francisco.
Local Favorites: When traveling to Peru, be sure to dive into the world-famous local cuisine. Be sure to try Peru’s national dish,: ceviche, along with other popular favorites like lomo saltado, causa, aji de gallina, and anything made with iconic andean potatoes.
Travel Tips: When searching for the best neighborhoods to stay in Lima based on preferences and budget, popular places include mid-range accommodation options in Miraflores, luxury hotels in San Isidro, and backpacker-friendly hostels in Barranco, which offer lively nightlife, exceptional dining options, and scenic coastal views.
Plan a stop in Lima with our Peru Tour Packages!
Cusco: Gateway to History and Adventure
Cusco offers the perfect blend of Inca history and Spanish colonial charm, serving as a gateway to Machu Picchu and the Sacred Valley. It’s a must-visit for history buffs and outdoor enthusiasts alike.
Cultural Must-Sees: Be sure to put iconic landmarks like Sacsayhuaman historical site and Q’enqo Archaeological Complex on your to-do list as well as vibrant markets where you can shop for local handmade Andean treasures.
For Adventure Seekers: Cuso offers a variety of adventures based on what you want to do and ability. Take a nearby short hike to Inca ruins like Tipon or a more adventurous multi-day trek in the Sacred Valley.
Traveler Tips: Cusco has a range of accommodations, from budget hostels to five-star hotels. This city is walkable, visitor-friendly, and the perfect stop with any of our tours to Peru.
Explore Cusco as part of your Peru adventure!
Lake Titicaca: Ancient Culture at the World’s Highest Lake
At an elevation of 3,821 meters, Lake Titicaca is the world’s highest navigable lake. This serene destination is a cultural treasure, surrounded by breathtaking views and vibrant traditions.
Cultural Experiences: Visit the floating reed islands (Islas Uros), Taquile Island, and engage with the Quechua and Aymara communities to experience the unique cultural aspects of this stunning location.
Scenic Highlights: Immerse yourself into the life in the picturesque villages of Llachon and Juli, as well as ancient ruins along the lake’s shoreline.
Travel Tip: Take the scenic train ride from Cusco to Puno and enjoy stunning Andean views during the journey.
Visit Lake Titicaca on our customizable Peru tours!
Arequipa: The White City at the Base of El Misti
Nicknamed “The White City” for its beautiful colonial buildings made of volcanic stone, Arequipa offers a romantic setting with rich history and cultural depth.
Why Visit Arequipa: If you love a charming town square, historic colonial architecture, and a relaxed, romantic vibe, Arequipa would be perfect for you! Arequipa was the colonial-era capital of this region and is surrounded by three towering volcanoes.
Top Activities: Explore the nearby El Misti volcano or enjoy the tranquil streets and cultural landmarks in the town center. Visit the Basilica Cathedral, wander around the Colca Canyon, see the Juanita Exhibit at Museo Santuarios Andinos, and take a local tour of the city.
Learn more about our Arequipa tour extensions!

summary: In some ways, life in the Amazon rainforest continues just as it did thousands of years ago. Both light and time seem unable to penetrate the near airtight canopy of towering trees sewn together with vines and moss.
full_text:
Amazon Jungle Travel
In some ways, life in the Amazon rainforest continues just as it did thousands of years ago. Both light and time seem unable to penetrate the near airtight canopy of towering trees sewn together with vines and moss.
From ancient bird-eating spiders to endemic monkeys that can sit on your fingertips, to thousand year old indigenous tribes still hunting with blowguns and spears, being in the Amazon feels like traveling back in time and every inch is energized with life.
Though tropical rainforests cover less than 10% of the Earth's surface, they account for over 50% of its species. One hectare of forest in the Ecuadorian amazon boasts about as many frog species as all of North America, and just one Amazonian tree can host more ant species than all of the British Isles combined. The Amazon Rainforest captivates anyone that has the good fortune of experiencing it's wonders.
Ecuador, with its 2% share of the Amazon basin (also known as the Oriente), provides unparalleled opportunities for experiencing the magic of the rainforest. Not only does it have one of the world's best developed infrastructures for rainforest tourism, but most destinations are accessible within a day's journey from Quito.
Whether you are looking for a luxury lodge with three-course meals and hot showers, a mud-up-to-your-knees trekking and camping adventure, or something in between, Ecuador has a program just for you.
There is no better complement to your Galapagos trip like a visit to the Ecuadorian Rainforest. We offer a variety of lodges and river cruises that provide top-notch services and are an excellent introduction to the Amazon.
Recommended Packing List
Binoculars
Flashlight (for night activities)
Camera
Water bottle
Insect repellent
Lightweight long pants and long sleeve shirts
Shorts and short sleeve shirts
Bathing suit
Comfortable shoes and extra socks
Small day pack
Lightweight rain jacket
Sunblock, sunglasses, and a hat
Amazon Jungle Travel Tips
Health
Although there is low risk for tropical diseases, it is always advisable to consult your doctor about taking precautions and getting vaccines. Please take any medications you may need with you.
Flights and Luggage
Flights from Quito to Coca and back are all done with modern airplanes from a national airline. Departure times are mid-morning. For the flight to Coca, the airlines require that checked luggage be limited to 44 pounds (20 kg) per person. Heavier equipment may be taken in carry-on bags if necessary.
Transportation to the Lodges
Normally guests will fly to Coca, then take a canoe to their final destinations. Canoes are usually covered to protect guests from the sun and rain, however, sunscreen is recommended while on the canoe to protect from the sun’s reflection off the water.
Weather
In the tropical rainforest it is best to be prepared for all kinds of weather. Common questions are usually about the “dry and wet season” within the region. However, it is best not to trust generalizations while planning a trip to the Amazon. At times it can be hot and sunny, but a cool rainstorm may appear at any moment. However, at night (especially after a rainstorm) it might get cold.
Clothing & Laundry
Lightweight pants and long sleeved cotton shirts are ideal for walks in the forest. Short-sleeved shirts can be worn with insect repellent. During a rainstorm, ponchos are recommended over full waterproof clothing, as it is warm and you will sweat a lot. Comfortable shoes (or sandals), shorts, and t-shirts are recommended for your stay. Please check our recommended packing list .
Laundry services may or may not be provided by your lodge, please check the details of your trip to plan accordingly.
Meals & Beverages
Lodge chefs are more than happy to prepare vegetarian, vegan, or other specialized meals for you upon request. Please make sure to advise your travel agent of any dietary requirements before you travel.
All lodges include meals except for alcoholic drinks , which are usually not included, however please check with your specific lodge for any exceptions.
Water in the lodges is purified, tested regularly, and safe for consumption.
Our Selection of Amazon Rainforest Lodges
Travel on board the M/V Anakonda, the only luxury ship in the Ecuadorian Amazon Rainforest, and experience the Amazon in a most unique way! Visit the remote and pristine areas where few have had the opportunity to travel, and interact with the region
Set on the banks of the Hollín River in Napo Province, this lodge has a privileged location within 30 hectares of protected Amazon rainforest. Every stay is designed to foster an authentic and responsible connection. Top experiences include immersive cultural encounters that create genuine interactions with local communities, as well as wellness journeys focused on mindfulness and inner renewal. For nature lovers, wildlife explorations deliver thrilling rainforest encounters, while a sensorial immersion program blends gentle trekking with activities that heighten awareness of the Amazon’s ecosystem.
Winner of the Ecotourism Award from the World Congress on Tourism and the Environment, La Selva Lodge sits high on Garzacocha Lake. The cabanas are constructed in the comfortable traditional native design. The delicious food is the pride of the lodge. There are a variety of excursions offered by the lodge with an English-speaking guide to explain the magnificent flora and fauna in the Amazon. La Selva is near a network of trails, a 135-foot observation tower and a large butterfly farm. The combinations of adventures are limitless. There is something for every person
With a premium location within Ecuador's Yasuni National Park, Napo Cultural Center features modern amenities and services while guests experience direct contact with the local community. This eco-conscious lodge immerses guests in facilities built with traditional Kichwa architecture showcasing their craftsmanship. The comfortable cabins feature cotton towels, linens, and hypoallergenic pillows. Each room boasts an ensuite bathroom and hot water heated through solar energy. Additionally, guests enjoy delicious meals prepared with seasonal and local ingredients, all while relishing the rainforest view of this Amazon lodge.
The Napo Wildlife Center is the most luxurious lodge in the Ecuadorian Amazon. The lodge consists of 16 cabañas and a large dining hall with a library and a well-stocked bar. Attached to the bar is a 50-foot viewing tower from which you can see the Andes on a clear day! To get to the Napo Wildlife Center, guests fly by jet from Quito to the town of Coca on the Napo River. From Coca you will take a motorized, covered canoe for a scenic two-hour trip down the Napo River. Upon arriving at the entrance to the NWC Reserve, we switch to small, dugout canoes and continue paddling up the black water creek to the lake and lodge.
The lodge is found within a 5000-acre private ecological reserve in Ecuador's Amazon region, an accessible yet pristine rainforest sanctuary where you and your family may enjoy a true jungle adventure in safety and comfort. The lodging at Sacha was carefully designed to offer comfort to the traveler yet preserve the environment and rainforest ambience. Guests may also enjoy a raised lookout above the main bar and lounge, which offers a scenic view of Pilchicocha Lake and excellent opportunities to birdwatch.
The Jamu Lodge is located on the Cuyabeno River, 15 minutes downstream from the marvelous Laguna Grande. The lodge offers the choice of a number of different programs that enable you to explore the jungle such as canoe rides to the primary forest or around the lake where you can see exotic trees and plants like orchids, bromeliads, and gardenias. Afterwards you can relax while sitting in a hammock or drinking an exotic cocktail at the bar.
Sani Lodge is truly a one of a kind Ecuadorian ecolodge dedicated to ecotourism, environmental conservation, and community projects in the Amazon rainforest of Ecuador. Sani Lodge is owned and operated by members of the Sani community meaning that with their extensive knowledge of the Amazon wildlife and biodiversity, they can give Sani Lodge guests the true experience of the Ecuadorian Amazon jungle. In addition to providing excellent service to its guests, Sani Lodge participates in community ecotourism - profits from the jungle lodge are reinvested into the community improving the lifes of all who live there.
Combining an Amazon Tour with your Galapagos Cruise
When traveling Galapagos it's important to be...
Dedicated. The Galapagos Islands are extremely remote, so it takes a dedicated traveler to get there in the first place.
An animal lover. Galapagos is like a zoo without walls, as it is known for its unique and fearless wildlife.
Adventurers. The Galapagos are not for those who want to relax on a beach; this "off the beaten path" destination is rugged, challenging, and above all, fun.
So if you're an adventurous, wildlife-loving traveler who's not afraid to go out their way to see something really special, I've got some great news for you! Ecuador is not only home to the legendary Galapagos Islands, but also the deep green jungle of the Amazon rainforest. A trip extension into the rainforest is easy to arrange and is the perfect complement to your Galapagos journey.
The Amazon is the largest tropical rainforest in the world and is home to a significant percentage of the world's wildlife and plant species. The forest teems with life, from the leaf-cutter ants on the ground to the parrots in the air. A single hectare of Amazon rainforest may be home to thousands of different species of plants, hundreds of insects and dozens of reptiles, amphibians and mammals. The Ecuadorian rainforest in particular is home for many birds: of the 9,000 or so birds that are known to science, some 1,500 of them are native to Ecuador.
The rainforest itself is a dense, living jungle. The rivers are fast, the air is humid and the thick green canopy dims the sunlight. The abundance of life makes for intense competition: plants grow on top of one another, clamoring for sunlight. Drop a banana peel on the ground and it will be gone within hours, carried off by ants and beetles for food. The treetops are alive with birds, monkeys and butterflies. Timeless cultures such as the Achuar people still live, hunt and fish the same way they have for millennia.
Ecuador's rainforest tourism industry is well developed and known for good service. Most of the animals live deep in the jungle, far from the cities, and therefore most visitors opt for a multi-day stay at one of the many remote rainforest lodges . A minimum stay is three days/two nights, but it's better to stay a little longer and fully take in the jungle. The lodges range from fairly inexpensive thatched-roof cabins to air-conditioned luxury camps with swimming pools and internet access.
However many stars your hotel has, a day in the jungle is similar everywhere. The lodges have guides, often natives who speak Spanish and English in addition to the local dialect. The guides lead informative hikes, pointing out medicinal plants, spotting camouflaged animals and treating visitors to special jungle experiences, such as snacking on lemon-flavored ants! Guided boat and canoe rides on the rivers and lakes are also popular: at night you can often see caimans, a relative of the alligator. On guided night hikes, you may see bats, scorpions and other fascinating insects and animals!
Many lodges make a point of giving back to local communities , hoping that tourism will replace other less sustainable industries such as hunting animals and birds to sell as pets. Some of these lodges are all or partly owned by the local community and the profits go to schools and social programs. Most lodges will at the very least offer tours of local communities.
Voyagers Travel Company works only with the most reputable lodges in Ecuador . Some of these lodges have decades of experience and have provided unforgettable experiences to thousands of visitors. The lodges vary according to price, location and level of comfort: you can even book a trip on a floating hotel which cruises up and down the Napo River (a tributary to the Amazon River)!
Don't let the adventure end in the Galapagos… ask your Voyagers Travel Company representative about an extension into the mighty Amazon!

Explore South America with Your Galapagos Vacation Package
In addition to the volcanic islands, white sand beaches, active wildlife, and turquoise waters of the Galapagos archipelago, South America has so much to offer. Experience more natural beauty, coveted cultural hubs, iconic food scenes, and immerse yourself into the best that South America has to offer in Ecuador and Peru. Here are some popular destination combinations:
Galapagos + Machu Picchu: Explore the Enchanted Islands in the Pacific Ocean, then journey to the ancient ruins of the Inca Empire. Built in the 15th century, this wonder of the world has dazzled and puzzled archeologists and tourists alike. Travel to the heart of the Incan empire to discover this hidden cultural mystery in the mountains.
Galapagos + Amazon Rainforest: Combine the diverse wildlife of the islands with the rich biodiversity of the remote Amazon rainforest in mainland Ecuador. Travel deep into one of the most remote places on the planet, known for breathing life into not just South America, but the world. Learn more about the communities that have integrated their lives with the natural wonders of this lush forest and discover the most biodiverse place on the planet per square meter; we guarantee you will see many different species of unique plants and animals in this natural laboratory.
Galapagos + Andes Mountains: Experience breathtaking mountain and volcanic landscapes alongside your Galapagos adventure. Travel to Quito, which is Ecuador’s capital, the old northern Incan Kingdom, and the first UNESCO heritage in the world that houses the best preserved Spanish colonial city in South America. Gaze upon the surrounding volcanoes that can be seen in every direction, including Cotopaxi, one of the largest active volcanoes in the world. Head a little bit north to Otavalo, to shop in the largest indigenous artisanal market in the Americas. Head to the east to Papallacta to soak in the natural hot springs of the mountains, this hidden gem is also known as the gateway to the Amazon where Pizarro started his expedition down the Amazon River. Or, head south to visit Chimborazo, the closest point on Earth to the sun.

Q: What’s the best time of year to visit the Galapagos Islands?
A: The Galapagos is a year-round destination . Whenever you choose to go on this unforgettable experience, you will surely see the diverse wildlife that the Islands have to offer, which includes sea lions, sea turtles, giant tortoises, blue footed boobies, Darwin finches, marine iguanas, and so much more!
Q: What’s the best time of year to visit Peru?
A: The ideal time to visit Peru is between May to October, as this is the driest time of the year and the best time to experience clear skies and less rainfall. However, since it is relatively close to the equator, you can travel any time of the year and still enjoy your adventure.

full_text:
Scuba Diving Galapagos: Liveaboard and Hotel Packages
Explore the Galapagos Islands’ legendary underwater world — home to whale sharks, hammerheads, marine iguanas, and rare pelagic life. Whether you choose a luxury liveaboard or flexible land-based package, your scuba diving adventure starts here!
View Our Diving Cruises
Dive Your Way: Liveaboard, Land-Based, or Combo
The ultimate option for serious divers. Access remote sites, dive multiple times per day, and live aboard a vessel designed for marine exploration.
Explore Diving Cruises
Stay in hotels on Santa Cruz or San Cristóbal Island and join daily dive excursions. Great for divers traveling with families or seeking flexibility.
Explore Diving + Hotel Packages
Blend diving with iconic land excursions to see blue-footed boobies, giant tortoises, lava fields, and more. Packages include lodging, activities, and inter-island transport.
Explore Land & Sea Combos
No matter how you explore, diving in the Galapagos Islands delivers unforgettable encounters beneath the waves.
What Our Divers Say
Liveaboard Diving Cruises: The Best Way to Dive the Galapagos
Liveaboard diving in the Galapagos is the gold standard for underwater exploration. These multi-day dive cruises, which usually last one week, are designed for experienced divers seeking unmatched access to remote sites, high-volume dives, and close encounters with the ocean’s giants.
Included in Most Liveaboards:
Access to Darwin & Wolf Islands, only reachable via liveaboard diving cruises
4 dives per day, including night and drift dives
Galapagos National Park-certified naturalist dive guides
Dive tenders, Nitrox availability, and onboard gear stations
Full-service cabins, meals, and expert-led dive briefings
Dive sites like Darwin and Wolf Islands, unreachable by day trip, make liveaboards the best way to experience Galapagos Islands scuba diving.
Legendary Dive Sites in the Galapagos Islands
Accessible only by liveaboard cruises, these sites offer massive hammerhead schools, whale shark sightings (June–November), and strong pelagic currents—ideal for advanced divers.
Located off Santa Cruz Island. Known for white-tipped reef sharks, eagle rays , and occasional hammerhead sightings in challenging conditions.
See marine iguanas feeding underwater, Galapagos penguins, mola molas, and seahorses. Cold water, deep dives, and advanced skill required.
Get Certified or Refreshed in the Galapagos
Galapagos Islands diving is best suited to certified and experienced* divers. However, land-based dive centers offer training and specialty options to help you prepare.
Options on Santa Cruz or San Cristóbal include:
PADI Advanced Open Water and Nitrox Courses
Refresher dives for certified divers returning to the sport
Specialty instruction on diving in cold water or strong currents
*Liveaboards typically require at least 50–100 logged dives and do not offer beginner training.
Plan Ahead for the Best Dive Experience
Due to conservation regulations, permits and liveaboard spots are limited. Booking 6–12 months in advance is strongly advised.
Secure your preferred dive vessel & dates
Avoid peak season sellouts
Unlock early-bird perks like gear upgrades or Nitrox inclusions
Want a Last-Minute Galapagos Dive Trip?
While most dive cruises fill early, last-minute openings are occasionally available due to cancellations.
If you're flexible, we can help you experience diving in Galapagos even on short notice!
Ready to Dive the Galapagos?
From world-class liveaboards to flexible land-based dive trips, we help you craft the perfect Galapagos scuba diving experience on your timeline, your style, and your terms.
Frequently Asked Questions
Q: Do I need to be an advanced diver?
A: Yes, especially for liveaboard cruises. Most cruise operators offering scuba diving in the Galapagos require advanced certification and 50–100 logged dives due to strong currents and deep dive profiles.
Q: Can I get certified to scuba dive in the Galapagos?
A: Yes! Once in the Galapagos, scuba divers can get certification through several dive centers that offer PADI Open Water, Advanced Open Water, and Nitrox courses on Santa Cruz and San Cristóbal Islands.
Q: Is dive gear included?
A: Most liveaboards and land-based shops in the scuba Galapagos scene offer full rental packages for an additional fee. Gear availability varies by operator, so we recommend confirming what you need in advance to ensure a smooth and fully equipped dive experience.
Q: When is the best time to go?
A: Diving in the Galapagos is a year-round opportunity, but each season brings unique marine life encounters and water conditions. Whether you're chasing whale sharks or looking for calm seas and vibrant reefs, understanding the seasonal patterns will help you plan the perfect trip.
Calmer seas and warmer waters
Higher visibility
Great for rays, reef fish, sea lions, and active reef life
Cooler water and strong nutrient-rich upwelling
Peak season for whale sharks, large schools of hammerheads, and marine mammals
Water temperatures range from 16–26°C (60–78°F). A 7mm wetsuit with a hood is strongly recommended year-round. For a broader overview of when to visit the islands, including wildlife calendars and climate tips, check out our full guide on when to go to the Galapagos .
Q: Are there last-minute dive tours?
A: Yes. While many trips book out in advance, we occasionally have last-minute availability for those flexible with their travel dates. If you're open to spontaneous diving in Galapagos, contact our team to check current openings and options.
Q: What should I pack for diving in the Galapagos?
7mm wetsuit with hood (especially June–Nov)
Dive computer and Surface Marker Buoy (SMB)
Reef-safe sunscreen and biodegradable toiletries
Motion sickness medication (particularly for liveaboards)
Underwater camera to capture once-in-a-lifetime encounters

Kayaking: Paddle alongside sea turtles and marine iguanas while you explore different island coastlines.
Snorkeling: Discover underwater marvels and play with the sea lions in crystal-clear waters.

FAQs: Your Questions About Galapagos Tours Answered
Q: What’s the best time of year to visit the Galapagos Islands?
A: The Galapagos is a year-round destination . However, based on the weather there is a dry season (June–November), which is a little cooler, that is preferred for diving and the wet season (December–May), which is a little warmer.
Q: Which is the cheapest way to visit the Galapagos?
A: There are many factors to include when determining the most affordable way to travel the Galapagos. Cruises for example are all inclusive, covering all meals, excursions and travel between the islands. Land-based tours may be more affordable, but may require additional costs. When trying to determine the most cost-friendly option, choosing between luxury, first-class, midrange, or budget would be the best way to go. Q: What’s the difference between a Galapagos cruise and a land-based tour?
A: Cruises access remote islands, offering an all-inclusive experience. Land-based tours provide stable accommodations on the islands and flexibility for exploring local areas. Click here to get a more detailed breakdown of different Galapagos Islands trips.
Q: Are Galapagos tours suitable for families with kids?
A: Both cruises and land-based tours offer family-friendly options. Activities like snorkeling, wildlife viewing, and gentle hiking are ideal for children, and guides are always present and happy to assist. Click here to learn more about family-focused Galapagos travel.
Q: Will I get seasick on a Galapagos cruise?
A: Galapagos cruises are designed for comfort but, thanks to mother nature, seasickness can occur depending on the tides and currents. If you’re worried about seasickness, but really want to go on a cruise , opt for a larger vessel or a catamaran, as it is more stable. Learn more about large v small boats here . Otherwise, a land-based tour may be a good option.
Q: Can I customize my Galapagos tour?
A: Galapagos Islands tours can absolutely be customized based on interests, budget, and travel schedules! To learn about all your options, consult one of our travel experts for more information about tailored itineraries.
Q: What wildlife will I see on a Galapagos tour?
A: No matter where you decide to visit in the Galapagos, you are guaranteed up close and personal diverse wildlife encounters in their natural habitats. Some of the most famous species are the giant tortoises, blue-footed boobies, marine iguanas, Galapagos penguins, and sea lions. It is important to note that some wildlife sightings depend on the island you visit and the time of year you visit. Depending on the month you visit the islands, different wildlife will be more active or present. Ask our experts about how you can travel to see what you want, whether that be whales, birds hatching, or the albatross returning to the Galapagos!
Still have questions? Contact our Galapagos travel experts now for personalized advice and assistance. We are happy to help you plan the trip of a lifetime!

Luxury Galapagos Cruise Experiences
Our luxury cruises combine exclusive remote island destinations with world-class comfort. Relax in spacious suites, dine on gourmet cuisine, and explore the Galapagos responsibly aboard vessels designed for minimal environmental impact. Experience the best of both worlds. Browse our luxury catamarans and cruises to the Galapagos Islands now!
What’s Included in a Typical Galapagos Islands Cruise?
Every Galapagos cruise is designed to maximize your experience with all-inclusive services, including:
Expert-led active excursions to remote islands by Galapagos National Park naturalist guides
Snorkeling gear and kayaking equipment included on most cruises (occasionally to rent on few cruises)
Gourmet meals and comfortable accommodations
Inter-island transfers
All shore excursions and activities with wildlife encounter and tours to local communities
Check out what a day in the life on a cruise looks like here !
Liveaboard Diving Cruises for Underwater Adventures
Dive into the Galapagos' underwater wonders with our liveaboard diving cruises. Explore world-famous dive sites like Darwin and Wolf Islands, home to whale sharks, hammerheads, sea turtles, and vibrant coral reefs. Live onboard your diving boat while you explore some of the best diving sites in the world where all your activities will be diving related! When choosing a liveaboard, you will be enjoying all meals and sleeping onboard these boats. These cruises are tailored for diving enthusiasts seeking the ultimate adventure.
Find Your Diving Cruise now!
How to Choose the Best Cruise to Galapagos Islands for You
Choosing the right Galapagos cruise depends on your voyage goals. Whether you’re looking for a family-friendly first class yacht, a romantic luxury cruise, or a budget-friendly adventure, we’ll help you find the perfect match. Things to consider:
Group size and preferences. Cruise boats in Galapagos range from about 16 to 100 travelers. It may be something to consider if you would like a more intimate experience where you would get to know all the passengers, or be on a larger ship where you can meet someone new every day!
Comfort level and amenities. Larger ships provide more stability and typically have more amenities. While smaller ships can anchor closer to land and you will receive more one-on-one attention.
Your budget and ideal cruise length. Cruises range from luxury to budget, so there is an option for anyone who wants to travel to the Islands regardless of budget constraints. Cruises also range from 4-8 days so you can truly find something that fits what you want!

Frequently Asked Questions About Galapagos Cruises
The Galapagos is a year-round destination . However, based on the weather , there is a dry season (June–November), which is a little cooler, that is preferred for diving and the wet season (December–May), which is a little warmer. Whenever you choose to go on this unforgettable experience, you will surely experience natural wildlife encounters that the Islands have to offer, which includes sea lions, sea turtles, giant tortoises, blue footed boobies, short eared owls, marine iguanas, and so much more!
Luxury cruises to the Galapagos Islands offer passengers a unique experience, providing guests with gourmet dining, spacious cabins, personalized service, and extra amenities onboard. Browse our selection of luxury catamarans and cruises to see if this is the best option for you!
Cruises absolutely cater to families and their needs, offering family-friendly itineraries and things to do. Activities like snorkeling, wildlife viewing, and gentle hiking are ideal for children, and guides are always present and happy to assist. Click here to learn more about family-focused Galapagos travel.
No matter where you decide to visit in the Galapagos, you are guaranteed up close and personal diverse wildlife encounters in their natural habitats. Some of the most famous species are the giant tortoises, blue-footed boobies, marine iguanas, Galapagos penguins, and sea lions. It is important to note that some wildlife sightings depend on the island you visit and the time of year you visit.
All meals and guided excursions to the islands are included in the price of your cruise. Typically all snorkeling equipment and gear are included on most cruises, and if not, they are available for rent. Things such as National Park fees, flights, alcoholic beverages, and tips may not be included. Feel free to reach out to one of our experts with any questions about a specific boat.
All Galapagos cruise operators follow strict National Park and international environmental practices, making environmental responsibility a priority. In addition, if you choose to travel with us at Galapagos Islands.Travel, we have our own environmental passion projects that you help support.
With a small yacht, you will usually have no more than 16 passengers abroad. This is best for guests looking for a more intimate environment and personalized service. Larger cruise ships typically offer more amenities and more stability for those prone to seasickness. Learn more about the differences here .
